title: Hodge decomposition of edge flows
purpose: Split a flow on the edges of a small graph (pairwise preferences, score differences, transfers) into a gradient explained by a global potential, curl circulating around filled triangles, and harmonic circulation around holes. Shows how much of a set of pairwise comparisons is consistent with a single ranking.

entry_points.name: hodge_decomposition
entry_points.arguments: nodes; edges: [[tail, head]] with one edge per node pair; flow: one number per edge; triangles: [[a, b, c]] 2-cells, or fill_triangles: true for every 3-clique
entry_points.returns: {gradient, curl, harmonic, potential, triangle_circulation, norms, betti_1, max_cross_product}

entry_points.name: flow_from_potential
entry_points.arguments: nodes; edges; values: one number per node
entry_points.returns: the flow values[tail] - values[head] on each edge

assumptions: The flow on edge (u, v) means flow from u to v; reversing an edge's orientation negates its value.
Which 3-cycles count as filled is a modelling choice: declared triangles or every 3-clique.
guarantees: gradient + curl + harmonic equals the flow; the three parts are pairwise orthogonal because B1 B2 = 0.
The curl and harmonic parts are divergence-free; the gradient and harmonic parts have zero circulation around every declared triangle.
A flow x_u - x_v is a gradient of the potential -x: its curl and harmonic parts are zero on any graph; potentials sum to zero on each connected component.

known_wrong.name: difference_flow_has_no_cycle_part
known_wrong.why: Pairwise differences x_u - x_v on a cycle look cyclic but are a gradient by construction; reading them as circulation is the trap.

limits: Dense least squares through pseudo-inverses: meant for graphs of up to about a hundred edges. Only 2-cells that are triangles are supported. The decomposition is unweighted; weighted HodgeRank (edge weights from comparison counts) is not included. It describes the flow; it does not test whether the curl part is statistically significant.
technique_references: Statistical ranking and combinatorial Hodge theory (Jiang, Lim, Yao and Ye)
Discrete Hodge decomposition on simplicial complexes
